references.text: Jethro advised Moses to choose capable men from among the people to serve as leaders and judges, which is a precursor to the appointment of the seventy elders.
Seventy of Israel's elders were called up on the mountain with Moses, Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu to worship the Lord.
The seventy elders went up and saw the God of Israel, a parallel to the selection of the seventy elders in Numbers 4.
Moses was asked to gather Israel's elders, showing that elders had an established leadership role in Israel.
The fulfillment of the command where Moses gathered the seventy elders, and they shared in the Spirit that was upon him.
Moses appointed leaders over the tribes, wise and experienced men, as part of organizing Israel's leadership.
The overseers (שֹׁטְרִים) of the Israelites are mentioned, the same word used for 'overseers' in this verse.
Jesus appointed seventy (or seventy-two) disciples, which can be seen as a parallel to the seventy elders that Moses appointed.
The apostles asked the congregation to choose seven men to serve, a similar delegation of responsibility as Moses was instructed.
